claims.author: luke-jr
claims.harm: parallelization could degrade rescan performance on non-SSD disks due to random I/O seeking
claims.quote: Have you benchmarked this on a non-SSD?

status_by.quote: I have measured it on an Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-7700 CPU with 8 cores, 64Gi RAM and a HDD

claims.status_note: author replied that fast rescan is CPU-bound on filter hashing, and l0rinc confirmed a 3x speedup on HDD

claims.author: bvbfan
claims.harm: scanning thread competing for mutexes and tasks could starve workers and slow down rescanning
claims.quote: All workers already process submit task in its own `WorkThread` just randomly trying to acquire mutex from scanning thread is non sense to me.

status_by.quote: I have changed the implementation so that the main thread only joins task processing when it needs to clear the work que

claims.status_note: author updated implementation so main thread only joins task processing to clear the work queue

claims.author: furszy
claims.harm: improve and separate the scanning code structure into a separate prerequisite PR before adding parallelization
claims.quote: I think it would be nice to first improve the current scanning code structure, then land the parallelization feature.

status_by.quote: I moved the test change into https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/34667 and the `ScanForWalletTransactions` refactor

claims.status_note: author split the refactoring into prerequisite PRs #34667 and #34681

claims.author: ismaelsadeeq
claims.quote: The current steps to reproduce in the description are stale because the commit hashes have changed since your force pushes.
claims.request: update reproduction steps in the description because the commit hashes have become stale

status_by.quote: The results have been updated in the PR description

claims.status_note: author updated the reproduction steps in description

claims.author: rkrux
claims.quote: These two conditions in this check seem redundant with the same two conditions in the following for loop.
claims.request: remove redundant conditions from the loop check

claims.author: rkrux
claims.quote: There is an overload method of `Submit` that accepts a range of tasks & pushes all of them in the queue within one acquisition of queue lock
claims.request: submit tasks in batches using the ThreadPool Submit range overload to reduce lock acquisitions
claims.status_note: author implemented ranged submission after rebasing

claims.author: rkrux
claims.harm: sharing a global threadpool across wallets could let a rescan controller thread process tasks from another wallet's RPC, distorting latency
claims.quote: Can't it happen that this controller thread picks up the task of another RPC of another wallet, thereby distorting results (from a RPC latency point of view) of this one?

status_by.quote: I have moved away from a shared ThreadPool to one that is initialized before scanning and discarded after.

claims.status_note: author moved from a shared threadpool to a dedicated one initialized per scan

claims.author: rkrux
claims.quote: It appears that `current_block_index + 1` is equal to `completed` due to a `int current_block_index = completed - 1;` above.
claims.request: simplify current_block_index + 1 expression since it equals completed

claims.author: polespinasa
claims.quote: As a small nit, I think there were some discussions about not creating more "result" enum types, and start using `Expected`. I think it would be cleaner to have a `ScanBlockError` type and return thos
claims.request: return util::Expected<void, ScanBlockError> instead of introducing a ScanBlockResult enum
claims.status_note: author changed return type to util::Expected<void, ScanBlockError>

claims.author: polespinasa
claims.question: ask whether combining block iteration and filtering is an intended behavior change
claims.quote: This is in fact a behavior change :)

status_by.quote: I updated the commit message to mention this second lookup. I also updated the comment.

claims.status_note: author clarified the behavior change and updated the commit message and comments

claims.author: polespinasa
claims.quote: nit: in many places you use `QueuedBlock` and in others you use a pair of `{block_hash, block_height}`. I think you could just use `QueuedBlock` always as it represents the same pair.
claims.request: consistently use QueuedBlock instead of a std::pair of block hash and height

claims.author: polespinasa
claims.quote: Maybe we should just throw here if `m_wallet_par` is negative? I think we should require `-walletpar` to be bigger than `-GetNumCores()` and smaller than `GetNumCores() + 1`. Also `GetIntArg` returns
claims.request: validate -walletpar bounds and prevent int64-to-int overflow from GetIntArg

status_by.quote: I've fixed the overflow issue, but the code still doesn't throw. I'm not convinced we need to throw here. I think silently using the maximum or minimum number of threads is good enough, rather than forcing the user to enter the correct num cores.

claims.status_note: author fixed the overflow issue but declined to throw on out-of-bounds -walletpar

claims.author: polespinasa
claims.harm: edge cases in parallel filter check could cause rescan to skip payments
claims.quote: There are a few ralph comments that I would say they are worth addressing. Specially in commit 5441a57e598628e94880ffcd455cecad70845e7e where there are some edge cases that can make the rescan skip payments.

claims.author: polespinasa
claims.quote: This shouldn't be uppercase. See https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/master/doc/developer-notes.md: "`Enumerator constants may be snake_case, or PascalCase. They should not be ALL_CAPS, according to the [C++ Core Guidelines](https://isocpp.github.io/CppCoreGuidelines/CppCoreGuidelines#renum-caps), to avoid clashing with macros.`"
claims.request: use enum class and avoid uppercase enumerator constants per developer guidelines
claims.status_note: author switched to enum class with proper casing

claims.author: polespinasa
claims.quote: In the case of IBD, if `m_wallet_par > 1` probably should log that the value of `m_wallet_par` was ignored.
claims.request: log that -walletpar is ignored when rescanning during initial block download
claims.status_note: author added logging when -walletpar is ignored during IBD

claims.author: w0xlt
claims.quote: Is there a reason to drop the anonymous namespace around FastWalletRescanFilter? The class is still only used inside scan.cpp. Keeping it preserves internal linkage and removes an unrelated change from this commit.
claims.request: keep FastWalletRescanFilter in an anonymous namespace to preserve internal linkage

claims.author: w0xlt
claims.quote: Now that ScanContext holds the per-scan state, LoopState seems redundant. LoopState's fields can be moved into ScanContext.
claims.request: merge LoopState fields into ScanContext to eliminate redundant struct
